To prove that the bees can fly home quickly from anywhere at all, even while stopping on the way for food.
To show how fast and impressive the return was, covering the distance quickly despite stopping for food.

distractors.text: To show that because the bees stopped to collect pollen along the way, they were able to get home very fast.
quotes: To show that because the bees stopped to get pollen, they got home really fast, in less than an hour.
distractors.refutation_sentence: I had released my insects at about two o’clock; these first arrivals had therefore flown two miles and a half in less than three quarters of an hour, and lingered to forage on the way.
distractors.why_not_single_sentence: The sentence joins speed and foraging with a plain "and", so matching its words seems to fit; the student must reason that stopping costs time, so it cannot be the cause.

distractors.text: To prove that the bees can fly home quickly from anywhere at all, even while stopping on the way for food.
quotes: To prove how fast and amazing the bees are, showing they can fly home quickly from anywhere even while stopping to get food.
distractors.refutation_sentence: Things being thus arranged, I carried off my forty captives to a spot two and a half miles from home.
distractors.why_not_single_sentence: The sentence does not negate "anywhere"; the student must notice that the test used one single release spot.

distractors.text: To show how fast bees in general can fly, since bees are quick fliers that cover long distances easily.
quotes: To show how fast bees can fly, since bees are really quick fliers and can go long distances easily.
distractors.refutation_sentence: Under the circumstances, I hardly thought, when I reached home, that the Bees would be there.
distractors.why_not_single_sentence: The sentence shares no wording with the option; the student must infer that the author doubted the bees could manage the trip, so it was not "easy".

key_support: I had released my insects at about two o’clock; these first arrivals had therefore flown two miles and a half in less than three quarters of an hour, and lingered to forage on the way.
Under the circumstances, I hardly thought, when I reached home, that the Bees would be there.

clusters.gist: To show the experiment was hard and imperfect: injured bees meant fewer could return
Even hurt bees could still find their way home, making the result more impressive
The bees were hurt and angry so they stung him
To show that marking the bees was hard and painful
He got stung and squeezed some too hard, so twenty got hurt (explains the injury, not the mention)
They could not navigate by landmarks seen from above, so they must have found home some other way
The author could not see where they went
Since they flew low the breeze got stronger and they could not see home
Bees do not need sight; they use a special sense, instinct or the sun
The wind made them fly close to the ground (restates the sentence)
